When I was preparing for a data‑engineering interview, the material I found was either too shallow or scattered across dozens of PDFs. I decided to consolidate the core concepts I needed—relational theory, table design, views, and optimization tricks—into a single, searchable GitHub repo.

The repo now contains concise lecture‑style notes for each topic, complete with examples that run on PostgreSQL and MySQL. I organized the content into separate markdown files, added a small index for quick navigation, and used GitHub Pages to render them as a lightweight reference site. The hardest part was distilling the nuances of indexing and query planning into a format that’s both accurate and easy to skim.

Since publishing, a few classmates have bookmarked the repo for their own study sessions, and I’ve already gotten feedback that the “Optimization Techniques” section saved them an hour of trial‑and‑error on a real query.

Repo link in comments. #SQL #DatabaseDesign
